newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Hanjin-Itochu bid lowest for Manila rail.
newsitem.headline: Hanjin-Itochu bid lowest for Manila rail.

text.p: A consortium comprising Itochu Corp and Hanjin Engineering and Construction Co has posted the lowest bid of 2.752 billion pesos for constructing part of Manila's new light rail project, a senior government official said on Friday.

Cesar Valbuena, assistant secretary for transportation and communications and head of the bids committee of the Light Rail Transit Authority, said bids by four other groups were higher and one bidder was disqualified for non-compliance of requirements.
He said due diligence was yet to be conducted and the contract will only be awarded next month.
Valbuena said Hyundai Engineering had posted a bid of 3.28 billion pesos while the D.J. Pumak consortium, comprising Filipino and foreign businessmen, had put in an offer of 3.383 billion pesos.
The winning bidder will construct the rail system's substructure and one underground railway station. Separate bidding will be held for laying tracks and constructing a depot.
Valbuena said a consortium of Kajima Corp and Samsung Corp bid 3.676 billion pesos while a grouping of Marubeni Corp, Balfour of the United States and DMCI Holdings Inc bid 3.685 billion pesos.
The bid by a consortium of Kumagai Gumi Co Ltd, Bechtel Corp of the United States and Philippine National Construction Co was rejected, he said.
The 14-kilometre line will extend from Recto Avenue in Manila to Santolan in suburban Pasig City. The metro is scheduled for commercial operation by 2000.
